RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 60

An all-male panel selecting a candidate with notably less formal leadership experience (courses versus your master’s and five years as deputy principal) raises legitimate concerns about implicit affinity bias. However, an all-male panel alone does not prove discrimination; appointments often hinge on interview performance, school-specific priorities, or references.

Rather than leading with the panel's composition—which may prompt immediate defensiveness—first follow up firmly on your written explanation, ideally with union or legal backing. If their documented rationale fails to objectively justify bypassing your superior leadership credentials, the unrepresentative panel composition becomes crucial corroborating context to support a formal gender discrimination or procedural grievance.
